decisions.reason: The piqué upholstery fabric dropped from its own page to a mere mention, a weak signal, but keeping a catalogue fabric costs little in a broad collection, so the option stays open for now.
The bouclé-effect decorative fabric remained listed through 2024, and since uncertainty about its demand is not yet resolved and carrying costs are low, holding the option is reasonable.
The flame-retardant jacquard serves the contract and hospitality market, has kept a dedicated page in both years and fits the firm's functional strategy, which signals value worth further commitment.

The double-face wool-blend fabric is still listed and matches the firm's push toward renewable materials, though it may face pressure if the firm reduces hard-to-recycle blends, so it remains an open option.
The wool bouclé leno fabric uses renewable fibre in line with the sustainability direction and is still listed, so the low-cost option is retained while its results unfold.

The braided-structure fabric was launched only in 2024 with its own page and versatile upholstery and curtain use, so its prospects are still highly uncertain and abandoning it now would be premature.
